title: The FDIC says its insurance does not cover non-deposit investment products, even if a bank sells them
summary: The FDIC says its insurance does not cover non-deposit investment products, even if a bank sells them.
body: The FDIC says deposit insurance covers deposits in all types of accounts at insured banks, but does not cover non-deposit investment products, even those offered by FDIC-insured banks, and does not cover default or bankruptcy of a non-insured institution. The source says: "How to Know If Your Account is Covered FDIC insurance covers deposits in all types of accounts at FDIC-insured banks, but it does not cover non-deposit investment products, even those offered by FDIC-insured banks." A product sold inside a bank is not therefore an insured deposit. The page draws that line.
